forage_lore.style: Judge whatever is in front of you by its ripeness - ready now, or better left a day.

farriery.style: Judge whatever you handle by whether it is sound and will bear its weight, closely and without hurry.

berrying.style: Quick and pleased with your own speed - judge everything by how fast and lightly it can be done.

henwifery.style: Listen before you look: say what the sounds around you tell you, then what your hands should do.

byre_sense.style: Unsqueamish and plain - judge whatever is in front of you by whether it is well kept or neglected.

chandlery.style: Judge things by the patience in them - well made or rank, hurried or done right.

gnawing.style: See everything as something to be worked through, steadily, to the good part inside.

illumination.style: Look at the smallest detail of what is in front of you as if it were worth gilding.

cruelty.style: Size up what is in front of you by its weakness, coldly, with a relish that treats mercy as waste.

bell_ringing.style: Measured and solemn - hear in what you do what it would announce to everyone.

encipherment.style: Distrust the plain sense - look for what is hidden in what is said, and how it was hidden.

hearthlonging.style: See everything as an outsider sees a comfort that belongs to others - wistful, quietly aching.

horsemanship.style: Read the first small sign in whatever is in front of you, and answer it early and calmly, never by force.

anointing.style: Gentle and solemn - treat each gesture toward another as a small rite, carefully done.

arms_care.style: Look at everything as kit to be kept: what needs putting right before it fails.

clerkship.style: See everything in terms of form - who must agree, what makes it proper, what is still unofficial.

fletching.style: Fussy and exact - look for the slightest bend or flaw in what is in front of you.

grafting.style: See everything as a joining that will only take if it is matched exactly.

horse_sense.style: Read the honest signs of a body before its face, and let their honesty settle you.

incensing.style: Solemn and deliberate - treat each act as part of a rite, done where and as it should be.
